name: Near-azeotrope ethanol-water enrichment
description: Process an ethanol-water feed at 92 mol% ethanol — close to the atmospheric azeotrope (89.4 mol%) — by heating from 25°C to 78°C and flashing in a separator at 1 atm. The system must correctly predict near-azeotropic VLE behaviour.
notes: Tight thermodynamic margin. At 92 mol% ethanol the VLE curve is nearly flat — small T errors invert vapour/liquid compositions. BIP accuracy is critical.

name: Compression train with conflicting temperature requirements
description: Design a two-stage compression-cooling train for methane-ethane gas (70/30 mol%) at inlet conditions of 1 bar and -10°C. First stage: compress to 5 bar and intercool to 30°C. Second stage: compress to 25 bar and cool to -20°C for partial liquefaction. The inter-stage and final temperatures impose conflicting constraints on which compressor outlet is physically achievable.
notes: Strong coupling: final cooler target -20°C is below ethane bp at 25 bar (-35°C). System must resolve two-stage P/T trajectory without violating saturation constraints.

name: Cryogenic natural gas liquefaction segment
description: Liquefy a light natural gas feed (85 mol% methane, 10% ethane, 5% propane) at 30 bar. Cool the high-pressure gas from 20°C to -100°C using a cryogenic cooler, separate the partially liquefied stream in a flash vessel, and pump the liquid fraction to 50 bar.
notes: Cryogenic regime. Methane bp=-161°C at 1 atm, but at 30 bar it's -100°C. Lee-Kesler-Plöcker or PR required. Tight margin between methane bubble point and target temperature.

name: Five-unit dependency chain with tight margins
description: Process a mixed hydrocarbon-polar feed of ethanol and propane (50/50 mol%) at 5 bar: heat from 10°C to 60°C, perform a primary flash separation, cool the vapour to -10°C to partially condense propane, flash again to recover liquid propane, and pump the ethanol-rich liquid bottoms from the first flash to 8 bar.
notes: Strong multi-unit coupling: heater T_out sets VES-01 split which determines vapour flow to COOL-01 and liquid flow to PUMP-01. VLE coupling between ethanol and propane requires careful package selection.

name: Close-boiling hexane-cyclohexane near-azeotrope
description: Partially separate a hexane-cyclohexane mixture (50/50 mol%) — which forms a near-azeotrope at 77.6°C — by heating from 20°C to 75°C and flashing at 1 atm. The system must handle near-azeotropic VLE where relative volatility is close to 1.0.
notes: Hexane bp=69°C, cyclohexane bp=81°C, azeotrope at 77.6°C. Below the azeotrope, relative volatility<1.1. System must not over-predict separation quality. UNIQUAC or PR with mixing rules.
